2024.dek: The year AI became a mass-market product and a capital-spending race: the figures that defined 2024 across usage, spending, finance, work, models, tokens, infrastructure, geography, industries, risk and regulation, each sourced, dated and rated. A retrospective edition, published November 2026.
2024.dek_plain: The figures that defined AI in 2024 across eleven themes, from ChatGPT's 300 million weekly users and $245 billion of big-tech capex to the EU AI Act's entry into force, each sourced, dated and confidence-rated.
analysis: 2024 was the year generative AI stopped being a novelty and became infrastructure. OpenAI said ChatGPT had 300 million weekly active users in December 2024, up from 200 million in August. McKinsey's 2024 State of AI survey found that 78% of organisations used AI in at least one business function, up from 55% a year earlier, and the American Medical Association found that 66% of US physicians used AI in their practice in November 2024, up from 38% in 2023. Adoption spread faster than any measure of return: the year produced many pilots and few audited results.

The money moved first into hardware. Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta spent about $245 billion on capital expenditure in calendar 2024, by Report AI's sum of their reported figures, and Nvidia's data-centre revenue reached $115.2 billion for its fiscal year ended January 2025, up 142%. Crunchbase counted more than $100 billion of venture funding to AI companies, about a third of all start-up investment, and Stanford HAI's AI Index put US private AI investment at $109.1 billion, nearly 12 times China's $9.3 billion.

Prices fell faster than almost anyone expected. Stanford HAI found that the price of GPT-3.5-level inference dropped from $20 per million tokens in November 2022 to $0.07 in October 2024, and Google said it was processing about 9.7 trillion tokens a month in spring 2024, a baseline that would grow more than 300-fold in two years. At the frontier, OpenAI's o3 preview scored 75.7% on the ARC-AGI-1 semi-private evaluation in December 2024, the first strong result on a test designed to resist memorisation.

The costs and the rules arrived together. The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with obligations phased in from 2025; US state legislatures introduced 635 AI bills and enacted 99, according to MultiState. The AI Incident Database recorded 233 incidents, and a deepfake video call cost the engineering firm Arup about $25 million. Challenger, Gray & Christmas counted 12,742 US job cuts attributed to AI, 1.7% of all announced cuts: real, but small next to what followed.

faq.q: How many people used ChatGPT in 2024?
faq.a: OpenAI said ChatGPT had 300 million weekly active users in December 2024, up from 200 million in August 2024. These are weekly users and should not be compared with monthly-user counts for other assistants.

faq.q: How much did big tech spend on AI infrastructure in 2024?
faq.a: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta spent about $245 billion on capital expenditure in calendar 2024, by Report AI's sum of each company's reported figures. Most of it went to data centres and AI chips.

faq.q: How much venture money went to AI companies in 2024?
faq.a: Crunchbase counted more than $100 billion of venture funding to AI companies in 2024, about a third of the roughly $314 billion invested in start-ups worldwide that year.

faq.q: What AI laws took effect in 2024?
faq.a: The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with its obligations phased in from February 2025. In the US, state legislatures introduced 635 AI-related bills in 2024 and enacted 99, according to MultiState; there was no federal AI statute.

faq.q: How many jobs did AI cut in 2024?
faq.a: Challenger, Gray & Christmas counted 12,742 US job cuts in 2024 that employers attributed to artificial intelligence, about 1.7% of the 761,358 cuts announced that year.

2025.dek: The year AI scaled faster than its returns: the figures that defined 2025 across usage, spending, finance, work, models, tokens, infrastructure, geography, industries, risk and regulation, each sourced, dated and rated. A retrospective edition, published November 2026.
2025.dek_plain: The figures that defined AI in 2025 across eleven themes, from ChatGPT's 800 million weekly users and $413 billion of big-tech capex to the first year of EU AI Act obligations, each sourced, dated and confidence-rated.
analysis: In 2025 AI became near-universal inside organisations and enormous outside them. OpenAI said ChatGPT reached 800 million weekly active users in October 2025, double the 400 million it reported in February. McKinsey's 2025 survey found 88% of organisations using AI in at least one business function, up from 78%. What people used it for shifted too: OpenAI's study of 1.5 million conversations found that 73% of ChatGPT consumer messages in June 2025 were unrelated to work, up from 53% a year earlier.

Spending grew faster than any revenue line could justify on its own. Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta spent about $413 billion on capital expenditure in calendar 2025, roughly 69% more than in 2024, and Nvidia's data-centre revenue reached $193.7 billion for its fiscal year ended January 2026. Crunchbase counted $202.3 billion of venture funding to AI companies, close to half of all start-up investment; OpenAI's $40 billion round at a $300 billion valuation in March was the year's largest. US private AI investment reached $285.9 billion, more than 23 times China's, according to Stanford HAI.

Usage of the models, measured in tokens, rose by orders of magnitude. Google said it was processing more than 1.3 quadrillion tokens a month in October 2025, up from 480 trillion in May, and OpenAI said its API handled more than 6 billion tokens a minute. Capability kept pace: Claude Opus 4.5 became the first model reported above 80% on SWE-bench Verified in November, and Gemini Deep Think earned an officially certified gold-medal score at the International Mathematical Olympiad in July. The IEA estimates that data centres used about 485 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025.

The costs became measurable. Challenger counted 54,836 US job cuts attributed to AI, more than four times the 2024 count. The AI Incident Database recorded 362 incidents, up 55%, and the FBI's first AI-specific tally counted 22,364 complaints and $893 million in losses. Rules started to bite: the EU AI Act's bans applied from 2 February and its general-purpose AI obligations from 2 August, US states enacted between 145 and 227 AI bills depending on the tracker, and by Report AI's count eight AI-focused US executive orders were signed.

faq.q: How many weekly users did ChatGPT have in 2025?
faq.a: OpenAI said ChatGPT reached 800 million weekly active users in October 2025, double the 400 million it reported in February 2025.

faq.q: How much did big tech spend on capital expenditure in 2025?
faq.a: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta spent about $413 billion on capital expenditure in calendar 2025, roughly 69% more than the $245 billion of 2024, by Report AI's sum of their reported results.

faq.q: How much venture funding went to AI in 2025?
faq.a: Crunchbase counted $202.3 billion of venture funding to AI companies in 2025, close to half of the $425 billion invested globally. PitchBook put AI's share at 53% and the OECD, using a broader definition, at 61%.

faq.q: How many US jobs were cut because of AI in 2025?
faq.a: Challenger, Gray & Christmas counted 54,836 US job cuts attributed to AI in 2025, 4.5% of the 1,206,374 cuts announced that year and more than four times the 2024 count of 12,742.

faq.q: What AI rules applied in 2025?
faq.a: The EU AI Act's bans on prohibited practices applied from 2 February 2025 and its general-purpose AI obligations from 2 August 2025. In the US, eight AI-focused executive orders were signed, by Report AI's count, including EO 14365 of 11 December 2025, which ordered a Justice Department task force to challenge state AI laws.

2026.dek: The year AI's scale met its bill: the figures that define 2026 so far across usage, spending, finance, work, models, tokens, infrastructure, geography, industries, risk and regulation, each sourced, dated and rated.
2026.dek_plain: The figures that define AI in 2026 across eleven themes, from ChatGPT's 1 billion weekly users and a $2.67 trillion spending forecast to the delay of the EU AI Act's high-risk rules, each sourced, dated and confidence-rated.
analysis: By 2026 the largest AI products had reached a billion people. OpenAI said ChatGPT had more than 1 billion weekly active users on 31 August 2026, and Alphabet said the Gemini app had more than 1 billion monthly users on 28 October; the two are different measures and cannot be ranked against each other. Inside organisations adoption has plateaued: McKinsey's 2026 survey found 89% using AI, but only 37% reporting any EBIT impact from it. Individual use at work is still rising, with Gallup finding 52% of US employees using AI at least a few times a year and 15% daily.

The spending is now measured in trillions. Gartner forecast on 16 September 2026 that worldwide AI spending will reach about $2.67 trillion this year. Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta spent about $508 billion on capital expenditure from January to September, more than in all of 2025, and their full-year guidance sums to roughly $720–740 billion. Crunchbase recorded $679 billion of global venture funding in the first nine months, about 72% of it to AI companies by Report AI's calculation. OpenAI raised $122 billion at an $852 billion valuation, and Anthropic's S-1 showed $16.3 billion of revenue in the first half and its first operating profit.

Tokens became the unit of the industry. Google said it was processing more than 3.2 quadrillion tokens a month in May 2026, about 330 times its spring-2024 volume. At GPT-4 quality, $1 now buys about 5 million tokens, roughly 188 times more than in March 2023, while the usage-weighted market price fell below $1 per million tokens in October. The build-out behind it remains concentrated: the United States received 78% of the AI compute added worldwide in the first half of 2026, according to Epoch AI, and Nvidia's data-centre revenue reached $89.0 billion in a single quarter.

The costs and the rules are both catching up, unevenly. Challenger counted 121,401 US job cuts attributed to AI from January to October, more than twice the 2025 total, although by November economic conditions had overtaken AI as the leading stated reason and a third of managers who cut roles for AI had rehired. A €95 million voice-clone fraud at Fideuram set a new record. The EU moved its high-risk AI rules to December 2027 and had published no AI Act fine by late September, while US states enacted 280 AI bills by early October. Returns are the open question: Wharton found 80% of enterprise leaders reporting a positive return, but only 28% a strongly positive one.

faq.q: How many people use AI in 2026?
faq.a: OpenAI said ChatGPT had more than 1 billion weekly active users on 31 August 2026, and Alphabet said the Gemini app had more than 1 billion monthly users on 28 October 2026. Weekly and monthly counts measure different things and cannot be added or ranked.

faq.q: How much is being spent on AI in 2026?
faq.a: Gartner forecast on 16 September 2026 that worldwide AI spending will reach about $2.67 trillion in 2026. Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta spent about $508 billion on capital expenditure from January to September 2026, and their full-year guidance sums to about $720–740 billion.

faq.q: Is AI making money in 2026?
faq.a: For the largest labs, increasingly: Anthropic's S-1 reports $16.3 billion of revenue in the first half of 2026 and a $974 million operating profit in the second quarter, and OpenAI's annualised revenue was almost $50 billion at the end of September. For users, the evidence is mixed: McKinsey found 37% of organisations reporting any EBIT impact, and Wharton 80% reporting a positive return but only 28% a strongly positive one.

faq.q: How many jobs has AI cut in 2026?
faq.a: Challenger, Gray & Christmas counted 121,401 US job cuts attributed to AI from January to October 2026, more than twice the 54,836 of 2025. AI-attributed cuts fell to 1,265 in October, and by its 5 November report economic conditions had overtaken AI as the leading reason year to date.

faq.q: When does the EU AI Act fully apply?
faq.a: The AI Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force since 27 July 2026, moved the AI Act's stand-alone high-risk obligations from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027. The Commission's power to fine general-purpose AI providers began on 2 August 2026; no fine had been published by late September 2026.

yoy.dek: 2024 vs 2025 vs 2026 to date, theme by theme: every comparable measure, how much it changed each year, and what the change means.
yoy.dek_plain: Year-over-year comparison of AI statistics for 2024, 2025 and 2026 to date across eleven themes: usage, spending, finance, work, models, tokens, infrastructure, geography, industries, risk and regulation.
analysis: Three years of data show AI accelerating in scale while several growth rates slow. ChatGPT's weekly users went from 300 million in December 2024 to 800 million in October 2025 and more than 1 billion in August 2026, but grew only 11% in the last six months of that run. Organisational adoption, as McKinsey measures it, rose from 78% to 88% and then stalled at 89%. Individual use at work kept climbing: Gallup's share of US employees using AI a few times a week or more went from 12% to 23% to 30%.

The money compounded. Big-four capital expenditure went from about $245 billion in 2024 to about $413 billion in 2025 and $508 billion in the first nine months of 2026. Venture funding to AI companies went from more than $100 billion to $202.3 billion and then about $488 billion in nine months, by Report AI's calculation from Crunchbase. The combined run-rate revenue of OpenAI and Anthropic rose from about $6.5 billion in December 2024 to about $115 billion in the third quarter of 2026, about 18-fold.

Prices and volumes moved in opposite directions, and so did costs and rules. The cheapest GPT-4-level tokens got 58% cheaper between 2024 and 2026 while Google's monthly token volume rose about 330-fold. AI-attributed US job cuts went from 12,742 to 54,836 to 121,401 in ten months of 2026, and incidents logged by the AI Incident Database from 233 to 362. Regulation moved from enactment to delay: the EU AI Act entered into force in 2024, applied its first obligations in 2025, and postponed its high-risk rules in 2026. Changes into 2026 compare a year to date or latest reading with a full year; each is marked.

faq.q: What grew fastest in AI between 2024 and 2026?
faq.a: Token volume: Google's monthly token processing rose about 330-fold, from about 9.7 trillion in spring 2024 to more than 3.2 quadrillion in May 2026. Combined OpenAI and Anthropic run-rate revenue rose about 18-fold over a similar period.

faq.q: Did AI adoption keep growing in 2026?
faq.a: Organisational adoption plateaued: McKinsey found 78% of organisations using AI in 2024, 88% in 2025 and 89% in 2026. Individual use kept growing: Gallup found the share of US employees using AI a few times a week or more rose from 12% to 23% to 30%.

faq.q: Are AI prices falling?
faq.a: At fixed capability, yes: the cheapest model of GPT-4 quality cost about $0.48 per million tokens in 2024 and about $0.20 in 2026 on a 3:1 input:output blend. At the frontier, list prices barely moved: OpenAI's flagship bought about 229,000 tokens per dollar in 2024 and about 250,000 in 2026 (Report AI calculations).

faq.q: Are AI job cuts rising?
faq.a: Annual totals rose from 12,742 in 2024 to 54,836 in 2025 and 121,401 in January to October 2026, according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas. The monthly count fell to 1,265 in October 2026, the lowest of the year.

faq.q: How are the year-over-year changes calculated?
faq.a: Report AI computes each change only where both years have a comparable value on the same definition; these are marked DERIVED. 2026 values are year to date or the latest reading, so a change into 2026 compares a part year with a full year where noted.

landing.dek: Eleven quarterly reports and an annual edition that put AI's figures in one place, each figure sourced, dated and confidence-rated, with free data to download and cite.
landing.dek_plain: The State of AI series from Report AI: eleven quarterly reports on AI usage, spending, finance, work, models and prices, tokens, infrastructure and energy, geography, industries, risk and regulation, plus the annual State of AI in Numbers and a year-over-year comparison.
analysis: The State of AI series is Report AI's set of named, dated reports on artificial intelligence, built to be quoted. Each of the eleven quarterly reports covers one theme: usage, spending, finance, work, models and prices, tokens, infrastructure and energy, geography, industries, risk, and regulation. Each opens with an executive summary of self-contained figure sentences, argues its case in chapters with numbered exhibits, compares 2024, 2025 and 2026, and ends with what to watch next.

Once a year the series is rolled up into State of AI in Numbers, the annual edition: one section per theme, written as a record of the year. The 2024 and 2025 editions were published as retrospectives in November 2026; the 2026 edition follows in mid-December. A year-over-year page puts every comparable measure side by side.

Every value carries its source, the date it describes and a confidence rating, and every report has a CSV download. Most figures are MEDIUM: they rest on consistent reputable reporting because many primary pages cannot be read directly from our research environment. Figures we compute are marked DERIVED and explained. Errors are logged in our corrections log the day they are fixed.

faq.q: What is the State of AI series?
faq.a: A set of eleven quarterly Report AI reports, one per theme (usage, spending, finance, work, models and prices, tokens, infrastructure and energy, geography, industries, risk and regulation), plus the annual State of AI in Numbers and a year-over-year comparison.

faq.q: How often are the reports updated?
faq.a: The theme reports are updated quarterly, with the edition named on each page (the current edition is Q4 2026). State of AI in Numbers is published each December, and the year-over-year page is updated with each edition.

faq.q: How should I cite a State of AI report?
faq.a: Use the citation line in each report's Cite this report box, for example: Report AI, State of AI Usage 2026, Q4 2026 edition, published 11 November 2026, https://report-ai.org/indexes/state-of-ai/state-of-ai-usage/.

faq.q: Can I use the data?
faq.a: Yes. Every report has a free CSV download with the source, date and confidence rating for each value, and the figures and charts may be quoted with attribution to Report AI and a link.

faq.q: How reliable are the figures?
faq.a: Each value is rated HIGH (primary source read), MEDIUM (consistent reputable secondary reporting), DERIVED (Report AI arithmetic, explained) or CONTESTED (credible sources disagree, both given). Corrections are logged publicly on the day they are made.
